VERIFIED MODEL PROFILE
Llama 3.2 · 3B
Start with the verified CPU profile. The suggested 8 GB system RAM budget includes headroom for the app and runtime.
GPU memory is optional. The verified profile currently runs on CPU.
ollama pull llama3.2:3b-instruct-q4_K_M
Memory guidance is a conservative estimate, not a measured minimum or a speed guarantee. Close other memory-heavy apps.

          
What about smaller models?
Llama 3.2 1B and Qwen3 0.6B are candidates for future profiles. They have not been validated with this codec, so downloading them alone won’t make them work in the local app.
Llama 3.2 1B · ~1.3 GB download ↗Qwen3 0.6B · ~523 MB download ↗

        

      


      
03 / OPEN THE LOCAL APP
A small setup. Then it’s yours.
Linux is the tested path.
Install Ollama, Python 3.10+ with venv, and Git. Then clone the project and run the launcher.
The launcher sets up Python dependencies, downloads the pinned model if needed, starts the dedicated runtime, checks replay, and opens the app.
A compatible llama-server is required. Some Ollama installations bundle it; others need it installed separately. The launcher checks this before downloading the model.
The current profile has been tested on Linux. Both servers stop when you exit the launcher.
TERMINAL
git clone https://github.com/jchook/plaintext-to-plaintext.git
cd plaintext-to-plaintext
./run-local.sh
Runtime paths, troubleshooting & manual setup ↗


      
Connecting other model backends
The codec needs repeatable next-token probabilities, exact token IDs and bytes, token-history control, and reversible tokenization. A chat-compatible endpoint alone does not establish compatibility.
The current adapter supports a pinned dedicated llama-server using a model downloaded with Ollama. Attach an already-running compatible endpoint with ./run-local.sh --url http://127.0.0.1:11535. The launcher checks identity and replay before opening the app.
Direct Ollama API support and more model profiles need adapters and their own round-trip tests. When added, each profile must identify the model, tokenizer, prompt, and sampling rules so the receiver can reproduce them.
